question: If an AI assistant can act before we ask it to, how do we make sure we still make the final decisions?
reflection: Helpful technology should give us back time and attention, while leaving the final choice in human hands.

sources.subject: Gemini 4 Neon, OpenAI Chip Model +14% PPA, Devin Bots
Claude Duet Wants to Be Your AI Chief of Staff. Is It Ready?

one_line: Personal AI assistants are becoming proactive, but the privacy and liability rules around them are still being written.

top_stories.title: Proactive assistants: helpful, but not yet reliable
top_stories.what: Forward Future tested Claude Duet, an assistant that reads email and calendars to spot work before you ask; it caught forgotten tasks but also made odd mistakes.
top_stories.why: How people decide when to trust a proactive assistant is a behavioural question that most AI companies are not measuring.

top_stories.title: Banks say customers carry the risk of AI agents
top_stories.what: Several large US banks now warn that customers may be liable for payments made by third-party AI agents, even if the agent is hacked.
top_stories.why: Liability is becoming the real brake on agent adoption; regulators and financial institutions everywhere will face the same question.

top_stories.title: AI starts to design the chips that run AI
top_stories.what: OpenAI and AMD reported that OpenAI's models improved the efficiency of an AMD GPU design by up to 14%, and some changes are already headed to manufacturing.
top_stories.why: AI is speeding up its own supply chain, which keeps pushing computing costs down for everyone who uses it.

saudi_lens.text: A new US rule requires licences to ship advanced chips to five countries where Chinese firms could rent computing power, so compliance is becoming a condition for any country that wants to be a trusted AI hub.
The bank liability debate is a preview for Saudi fintech and open banking: who is responsible when an AI agent pays on a customer's behalf will need a clear local answer.

idea.title: Trust calibration study for AI assistants
idea.pitch: Test which cues (confidence scores, explanations, asking permission) help people accept an assistant's good suggestions and reject its bad ones.
idea.fit: Government digital services, banks and fintech, health
idea.first_step: Draft 10 assistant suggestions, half correct and half wrong, and design two versions of how they are presented.

terms.definition: An AI assistant that notices what needs doing from your email, calendar or files and offers to do it, instead of waiting for a request.
How well a person's trust in a system matches how reliable it really is: trusting it when it is right and doubting it when it is wrong.
Government rules that limit which countries or companies may buy certain technologies, such as advanced AI chips.

concepts.summary: Assistants that watch your work and offer to act before being asked.
Who pays when an AI agent acting for a person makes a mistake or is hacked.
Using AI models to improve the design of the processors that run AI.
